name: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model
purpose: A way for a civilian agency to say how far along zero trust it is, and what the next stage looks like.
what: Five pillars, three cross-cutting capabilities and four stages: Traditional, Initial, Advanced and Optimal. Each pillar’s functions are described at every stage.

binds.line: Written for federal civilian agencies. It binds only through OMB M-22-09, whose goals it organizes.

verifiedBy.line: Agencies place themselves on the stages. The memo, not the model, carried the deadline, which passed in 2024.

sits.line: Layer 3. A maturity model: it describes the target state in stages.

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026: the resource page prints ‘Revision Date April 11, 2023’ and lists Version 2.0 as the only edition. The tables were extracted by script from the PDF that page links (Tables 2 to 7, pages 13 to 30) and compared with a second extraction: 22 functions in the five pillars, the three cross-cutting capabilities as rows of every pillar and as a table of their own, four stages each, 160 descriptions in all, none empty. Footnote marks are left out. Page 8 speaks of three stages after a Traditional starting point; the tables have four columns.

terms.line: A work of the United States government. Lensatic shows CISA’s pillars, functions and stage descriptions as Version 2.0 prints them. CISA gives them no identifiers.

related.line: The model builds on SP 800-207’s definition.
The {{dow}} counterpart: seven pillars and a dated Target Level.

depth.unit: functions and capabilities, each at four stages

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency authenticates identity using either passwords or multi-factor authentication (MFA) with static access for entity identity.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency authenticates identity using MFA, which may include passwords as one factor and requires validation of multiple entity attributes (e.g., locale or activity).

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency begins to authenticate all identity using phishing-resistant MFA and attributes, including initial implementation of password-less MFA via FIDO2 or PIV.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency continuously validates identity with phishing-resistant MFA, not just when access is initially granted.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency only uses self-managed, on-premises (i.e., planned, deployed, and maintained by agency) identity stores.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency has a combination of self-managed identity stores and hosted identity store(s) (e.g., cloud or other agency) with minimal integration between the store(s) (e.g., Single Sign-on.).

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency begins to securely consolidate and integrate some self-managed and hosted identity stores.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency securely integrates their identity stores across all partners and environments as appropriate.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency makes limited determinations for identity risk (i.e., likelihood that an identity is compromised).

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency determines identity risk using manual methods and static rules to support visibility.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency determines identity risk with some automated analysis and dynamic rules to inform access decisions and response activities.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency determines identity risk in real time based on continuous analysis and dynamic rules to deliver ongoing protection.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency authorizes permanent access with periodic review for both privileged and unprivileged accounts.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency authorizes access, including for privileged access requests, that expires with automated review.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency authorizes need-based and session-based access, including for privileged access request, that is tailored to actions and resources.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency uses automation to authorize just-in-time and just-enough access tailored to individual actions and individual resource needs.

nodes.title: Visibility and Analytics Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency collects user and entity activity logs, especially for privileged credentials, and performs some routine manual analysis.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency collects user and entity activity logs and performs routine manual analysis and some automated analysis, with limited correlation between log types.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency performs automated analysis across some user and entity activity log types and augments collection to address gaps in visibility.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency maintains comprehensive visibility and situational awareness across enterprise by performing automated analysis over user activity log types, including behavior-based analytics.

nodes.title: Automation and Orchestration Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency manually orchestrates (onboards, offboards, and disables) self-managed identities (users and entities), with little integration, and performs regular review.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency manually orchestrates privileged and external identities and automates orchestration of non-privileged users and of self-managed entities.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency manually orchestrates privileged user identities and automates orchestration of all identities with integration across all environments.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency automates orchestration of all identities with full integration across all environments based on behaviors, enrollments, and deployment needs.

nodes.title: Governance Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency implements identity policies (authentication, credentials, access, lifecycle, etc.) with enforcement via static technical mechanisms and manual review.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency defines and begins implementing identity policies for enterprise-wide enforcement with minimal automation and manual updates.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency implements identity policies for enterprise-wide enforcement with automation and updates policies periodically.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency implements and fully automates enterprise-wide identity policies for all users and entities across all systems with continuous enforcement and dynamic updates.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency has limited, if any, visibility (i.e., ability to inspect device behavior) into device compliance with few methods of enforcing policies or managing software, configurations, or vulnerabilities.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency receives self-reported device characteristics (e.g., keys, tokens, users, etc., on the device) but has limited enforcement mechanisms. Agency has a preliminary, basic process in place to approve software use and push updates and configuration changes to devices.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency has verified insights (i.e., an administrator can inspect and verify the data on device) on initial access to device and enforces compliance for most devices and virtual assets. Agency uses automated methods to manage devices and virtual assets, approve software, and identify vulnerabilities and install patches.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency continuously verifies insights and enforces compliance throughout the lifetime of devices and virtual assets. Agency integrates device, software, configuration, and vulnerability management across all agency environments, including for virtual assets.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency does not track physical or virtual assets in an enterprise-wide or cross-vendor manner and manages its own supply chain acquisition of devices and services in ad hoc fashion with a limited view of enterprise risks.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency tracks all physical and some virtual assets and manages supply chain risks by establishing policies and control baselines according to federal recommendations using a robust framework, (e.g., NIST SCRM.)

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency begins to develop a comprehensive enterprise view of physical and virtual assets via automated processes that can function across multiple vendors to verify acquisitions, track development cycles, and provide third-party assessments.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency has a comprehensive, at- or near-real-time view of all assets across vendors and service providers, automates its supply chain risk management as applicable, builds operations that tolerate supply chain failures, and incorporates best practices.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency does not require visibility into devices or virtual assets used to access resources.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency requires some devices or virtual assets to report characteristics then use this information to approve resource access.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency’s initial resource access considers verified device or virtual asset insights.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency’s resource access considers real-time risk analytics within devices and virtual assets.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency manually deploys threat protection capabilities to some devices.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency has some automated processes for deploying and updating threat protection capabilities to devices and to virtual assets with limited policy enforcement and compliance monitoring integration.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency begins to consolidate threat protection capabilities to centralized solutions for devices and virtual assets and integrates most of these capabilities with policy enforcement and compliance monitoring.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency has a centralized threat protection security solution(s) deployed with advanced capabilities for all devices and virtual assets and a unified approach for device threat protection, policy enforcement, and compliance monitoring.

nodes.title: Visibility and Analytics Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency uses a physically labeled inventory and limited software monitoring to review devices on a regular basis with some manual analysis.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency uses digital identifiers (e.g., interface addresses, digital tags) alongside a manual inventory and endpoint monitoring of devices when available. Some agency devices and virtual assets are under automated analysis (e.g., software-based scanning) for anomaly detection based on risk.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency automates both inventory collection (including endpoint monitoring on all standard user devices, e.g., desktops and laptops, mobile phones, tablets, and their virtual assets) and anomaly detection to detect unauthorized devices.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency automates status collection of all network-connected devices and virtual assets while correlating with identities, conducting endpoint monitoring, and performing anomaly detection to inform resource access. Agency tracks patterns of provisioning and/or de-provisioning of virtual assets for anomalies.

nodes.title: Automation and Orchestration Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency manually provisions, configures, and/or registers devices within the enterprise.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins to use tools and scripts to automate the process of provisioning, configuration, registration, and/or deprovisioning for devices and virtual assets.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency has implemented monitoring and enforcement mechanisms to identify and manually disconnect or isolate non-compliant (vulnerable, unverified certificate; unregistered mac address) devices and virtual assets.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency has fully automated processes for provisioning, registering, monitoring, isolating, remediating, and deprovisioning devices and virtual assets.

nodes.title: Governance Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency sets some policies for the lifecycle of their traditional and peripheral computing devices and relies on manual processes to maintain (e.g., update, patch, sanitize) these devices.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency sets and enforces policies for the procurement of new devices, the lifecycle of non-traditional computing devices and virtual assets, and for regularly conducting monitoring and scanning of devices.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency sets enterprise-wide policies for the lifecycle of devices and virtual assets, including their enumeration and accountability, with some automated enforcement mechanisms.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency automates policies for the lifecycle of all network-connected devices and virtual assets across the enterprise.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency defines their network architecture using large perimeter/macro-segmentation with minimal restrictions on reachability within network segments. Agency may also rely on multi-service interconnections (e.g., bulk traffic VPN tunnels).

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins to deploy network architecture with the isolation of critical workloads, constraining connectivity to least function principles, and a transition toward service-specific interconnections.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency expands deployment of endpoint and application profile isolation mechanisms to more of their network architecture with ingress/egress micro-perimeters and service-specific interconnections.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency network architecture consists of fully distributed ingress/egress micro-perimeters and extensive micro-segmentation based around application profiles with dynamic just-in-time and just-enough connectivity for service-specific interconnections.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency manually implements static network rules and configurations to manage traffic at service provisioning, with limited monitoring capabilities (e.g., application performance monitoring or anomaly detection) and manual audits and reviews of profile changes for mission critical applications.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency establishes application profiles with distinct traffic management features and begins to map all applications to these profiles. Agency expands application of static rules to all applications and performs periodic manual audits of application profile assessments.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency implements dynamic network rules and configurations for resource optimization that are periodically adapted based upon automated risk-aware and risk-responsive application profile assessments and monitoring.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency implements dynamic network rules and configurations that continuously evolve to meet application profile needs and reprioritize applications based on mission criticality, risk, etc.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency encrypts minimal traffic and relies on manual or ad hoc processes to manage and secure encryption keys.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins to encrypt all traffic to internal applications, to prefer encryption for traffic to external applications, to formalize key management policies, and to secure server/service encryption keys.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency ensures encryption for all applicable internal and external traffic protocols, manages issuance and rotation of keys and certificates, and begins to incorporate best practices for cryptographic agility.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency continues to encrypt traffic as appropriate, enforces least privilege principles for secure key management enterprise-wide, and incorporates best practices for cryptographic agility as widely as possible.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency configures network capabilities on a case-by-case basis to only match individual application availability demands with limited resilience mechanisms for workloads not deemed mission critical.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins to configure network capabilities to manage availability demands for additional applications and expand resilience mechanisms for workloads not deemed mission critical.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency has configured network capabilities to dynamically manage the availability demands and resilience mechanisms for the majority of their applications.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency integrates holistic delivery and awareness in adapting to changes in availability demands for all workloads and provides proportionate resilience.

nodes.title: Visibility and Analytics Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency incorporates limited boundary-focused network monitoring capabilities with minimal analysis to start developing centralized situational awareness.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency employs network monitoring capabilities based on known indicators of compromise (including network enumeration) to develop situational awareness in each environment and begins to correlate telemetry across traffic types and environments for analysis and threat hunting activities.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency deploys anomaly-based network detection capabilities to develop situational awareness across all environments, begins to correlate telemetry from multiple sources for analysis, and incorporates automated processes for robust threat hunting activities.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency maintains visibility into communication across all agency networks and environments while enabling enterprise-wide situational awareness and advanced monitoring capabilities that automate telemetry correlation across all detection sources.

nodes.title: Automation and Orchestration Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency uses manual processes to manage the configuration and resource lifecycle for agency networks and environments with periodic integration of policy requirements and situational awareness.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins using automated methods to manage the configuration and resource lifecycle for some agency networks or environments and ensures that all resources have a defined lifetime based on policies and telemetry.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency uses automated change management methods (e.g., CI/CD) to manage the configuration and resource lifecycle for all agency networks and environments, responding to and enforcing policies and protections against perceived risks.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency networks and environments are defined using infrastructure-as-code managed by automated change management methods, including automated initiation and expiration to align with changing needs.

nodes.title: Governance Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency implements static network policies (access, protocols, segmentation, alerts, and remediation) with an approach focused on perimeter protections.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency defines and begins to implement policies tailored to individual network segments and resources while also inheriting corporate-wide rules as appropriate.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency incorporates automation in implementing tailored policies and facilitates the transition from perimeter-focused protections.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency implements enterprise-wide network policies that enable tailored, local controls; dynamic updates; and secure external connections based on application and user workflows.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency authorizes access to applications primarily based on local authorization and static attributes.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins to implement authorizing access capabilities to applications that incorporate contextual information (e.g., identity, device compliance, and/or other attributes) per request with expiration.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency automates application access decisions with expanded contextual information and enforced expiration conditions that adhere to least privilege principles.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency continuously authorizes application access, incorporating real-time risk analytics and factors such as behavior or usage patterns.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency threat protections have minimal integration with application workflows, applying general purpose protections for known threats.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency integrates threat protections into mission critical application workflows, applying protections against known threats and some application-specific threats.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency integrates threat protections into all application workflows, protecting against some application-specific and targeted threats.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency integrates advanced threat protections into all application workflows, offering real-time visibility and content-aware protections against sophisticated attacks tailored to applications.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency makes some mission critical applications available only over private networks and protected public network connections (e.g., VPN) with monitoring.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency makes some of their applicable mission critical applications available over open public networks to authorized users with need via brokered connections.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency makes most of their applicable mission critical applications available over open public network connections to authorized users as needed.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency makes all applicable applications available over open public networks to authorized users and devices, where appropriate, as needed.

nodes.title: Secure Application Development and Deployment Workflow
Traditional
nodes.text: Agency has ad hoc development, testing, and production environments with non-robust code deployment mechanisms.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency provides infrastructure for development, testing, and production environments (including automation) with formal code deployment mechanisms through CI/CD pipelines and requisite access controls in support of least privilege principles.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency uses distinct and coordinated teams for development, security, and operations while removing developer access to production environment for code deployment.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency leverages immutable workloads where feasible, only allowing changes to take effect through redeployment, and removes administrator access to deployment environments in favor of automated processes for code deployment.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency performs application security testing prior to deployment, primarily via manual testing methods.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins to use static and dynamic (i.e., application is executing) testing methods to perform security testing, including manual expert analysis, prior to application deployment.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency integrates application security testing into the application development and deployment process, including the use of periodic dynamic testing methods.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency integrates application security testing throughout the software development lifecycle across the enterprise with routine automated testing of deployed applications.

nodes.title: Visibility and Analytics Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency performs some performance and security monitoring of mission critical applications with limited aggregation and analytics.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins to automate application profile (e.g., state, health, and performance) and security monitoring for improved log collection, aggregation, and analytics.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency automates profile and security monitoring for most applications with heuristics to identify application-specific and enterprise-wide trends and refines processes over time to address gaps in visibility.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency performs continuous and dynamic monitoring across all applications to maintain enterprise-wide comprehensive visibility.

nodes.title: Automation and Orchestration Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency manually establishes static application hosting location and access at provisioning with limited maintenance and review.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency periodically modifies application configurations (including location and access) to meet relevant security and performance goals.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency automates application configurations to respond to operational and environmental changes.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency automates application configurations to continuously optimize for security and performance.

nodes.title: Governance Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency relies primarily on manual enforcement policies for application access, development, deployment, software asset management, security testing and evaluation (ST&E) at technology insertion, patching, and tracking software dependencies.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins to automate policy enforcement for application development (including access to development infrastructure), deployment, software asset management, ST&E at technology insertion, patching, and tracking software dependencies based upon mission needs (for example, with Software Bill of Materials).

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency implements tiered, tailored policies enterprise-wide for applications and all aspects of the application development and deployment lifecycles and leverages automation, where possible, to support enforcement.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency fully automates policies governing applications development and deployment, including incorporating dynamic updates for applications through the CI/CD pipeline.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency manually identifies and inventories some agency data (e.g., mission critical data).

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins to automate data inventory processes for both on-premises and in cloud environments, covering most agency data, and begins to incorporate protections against data loss.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency automates data inventory and tracking enterprise-wide, covering all applicable agency data, with data loss prevention strategies based upon static attributes and/or labels.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency continuously inventories all applicable agency data and employs robust data loss prevention strategies that dynamically block suspected data exfiltration.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency employs limited and ad hoc data categorization capabilities.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins to implement a data categorization strategy with defined labels and manual enforcement mechanisms.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency automates some data categorization and labeling processes in a consistent, tiered, targeted manner with simple, structured formats and regular review.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency automates data categorization and labeling enterprise-wide with robust techniques; granular, structured formats; and mechanisms to address all data types.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency primarily makes data available from on-premises data stores with some off-site backups.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency makes some data available from redundant, highly available data stores (e.g., cloud) and maintains off-site backups for on-premises data.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency primarily makes data available from redundant, highly available data stores and ensures access to historical data.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency uses dynamic methods to optimize data availability, including historical data, according to user and entity need.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency governs user and entity access (e.g., permissions to read, write, copy, grant others access, etc.) to data through static access controls.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins to deploy automated data access controls that incorporate elements of least privilege across the enterprise.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency automates data access controls that consider various attributes such as identity, device risk, application, data category, etc., and are time limited where applicable.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency automates dynamic just-in-time and just-enough data access controls enterprise-wide with continuous review of permissions.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency encrypts minimal agency data at rest and in transit and relies on manual or ad hoc processes to manage and secure encryption keys.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency encrypts all data in transit and, where feasible, data at rest (e.g., mission critical data and data stored in external environments) and begins to formalize key management policies and secure encryption keys.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency encrypts all data at rest and in transit across the enterprise to the maximum extent possible, begins to incorporate cryptographic agility, and protects encryption keys (i.e., secrets are not hard coded and are rotated on a regular basis).

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency encrypts data in use where appropriate, enforces least privilege principles for secure key management enterprise-wide, and applies encryption using up-to-date standards and cryptographic agility to the extent possible.

nodes.title: Visibility and Analytics Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency has limited visibility into data including location, access, and usage, with analysis consisting primarily of manual processes.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency obtains visibility based on data inventory management, categorization, encryption, and access attempts, with some automated analysis and correlation.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency maintains data visibility in a more comprehensive, enterprise-wide manner with automated analysis and correlation and begins to employ predictive analytics.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency has visibility across the full data lifecycle with robust analytics, including predictive analytics, that support comprehensive views of agency data and continuous security posture assessment.

nodes.title: Automation and Orchestration Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency implements data lifecycle and security policies (e.g., access, usage, storage, encryption, configurations, protections, backups, categorization, sanitization) through manual, and potentially ad hoc, processes.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency uses some automated processes to implement data lifecycle and security policies.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency implements data lifecycle and security policies primarily through automated methods for most agency data in a consistent, tiered, targeted manner across the enterprise.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency automates, to the maximum extent possible, data lifecycles and security policies for all agency data across the enterprise.

nodes.title: Governance Capability
nodes.note: A cross-cutting capability, as it applies in this pillar.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency relies on ad hoc data governance policies (e.g., for protection, categorization, access, inventorying, storage, recovery, removal, etc.) with manual implementation.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency defines high-level data governance policies and relies primarily on manual, segmented implementation.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency begins integration of data lifecycle policy enforcement across the enterprise, enabling more unified definitions for data governance policies.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency data lifecycle policies are unified to the maximum extent possible and dynamically enforced across the enterprise.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency manually collects limited logs across their enterprise with low fidelity and minimal analysis.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins to automate the collection and analysis of logs and events for mission critical functions and regularly assesses processes for gaps in visibility.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency expands the automated collection of logs and events enterprise-wide (including virtual environments) for centralized analysis that correlates across multiple sources.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency maintains comprehensive visibility enterprise-wide via centralized dynamic monitoring and advanced analysis of logs and events.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency relies on static and manual processes to orchestrate operations and response activities with limited automation.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency begins automating orchestration and response activities in support of critical mission functions.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency automates orchestration and response activities enterprise-wide, leveraging contextual information from multiple sources to inform decisions.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency orchestration and response activities dynamically respond to enterprise-wide changing requirements and environmental changes.

nodes.title: Traditional
nodes.text: Agency implements policies in an ad hoc manner across the enterprise, with policies enforced via manual processes or static technical mechanisms.

nodes.title: Initial
nodes.text: Agency defines and begins implementing policies for enterprise-wide enforcement with minimal automation and manual updates.

nodes.title: Advanced
nodes.text: Agency implements tiered, tailored policies enterprise-wide and leverages automation where possible to support enforcement. Access policy decisions incorporate contextual information from multiple sources.

nodes.title: Optimal
nodes.text: Agency implements and fully automates enterprise-wide policies that enable tailored local controls with continuous enforcement and dynamic updates.
